Both posts declare indexed work offsets with a maximum of six. The conversion writes G54 through G59. The engine validates the index before each script receives it. The change meets issue #1385.

Safety checks: I restored each old script separately in the local review worktree. The declaration test failed with `grblhal.cps declares workOffsetIndex`, then with `tinyg.cps declares workOffsetIndex`. Each mutation returned exit 101. After each restoration, all nine `work_offset_index` tests passed.

The offset suite checks valid output, the maximum refusal, display names, and legacy word input. No goldens moved. Both recorded script suites passed against the unchanged goldens. No UI files changed. No controller or machine run was made.

Requested before merge: none.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
Follow-up process fix filed as #1828: /merge-ready must not offer a PR whose only review marker is the author's own.

Retro review (merged): sound

This is a read-after-merge review of PR #1824. It ran at merge commit a330f7cbd.

**What I read**
- The PR body and full diff.
- Issue #1385.
- `crates/post/src/post/work_offset.rs` and the engine's `WorkOffset` path in `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs`.
- `assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, `assets/posts/tinyg.cps`, and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`.
- `crates/post/tests/work_offset_index.rs` and `docs/decisions/1385-indexed-offsets.md`.

**What I built (local worktree, runner not used)**
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (full): 518 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No app suites ran. The diff does not touch `crates/app`.

**Law checks (posted-G-code safety floor)**
- The engine translates every `PARAM WorkOffset` before a script sees it (engine.rs:163). A bad value and an index above the declared maximum are refused by setup name (work_offset.rs:87-109). A script cannot receive a value that writes a wrong word.
- `workOffsetName` returns `"G" + (53 + n)` with n in 1..=6 (grblhal.cps:298, tinyg.cps:295; both declare `workOffsetMax = 6`). This writes the same G54..G59 words as the old legacy path. The default `wcsWord = "G54"` is unchanged. No existing machine's output changes.
- A stream that carries a legacy word reads as its index first (work_offset.rs:34-49), so the script still receives a whole number. The test `a_legacy_word_in_the_stream_reads_as_its_index` proves this for all 13 scripts.
- Other shipped scripts did not change. An unflagged script keeps the old word path.
- The new scripts append to `SCRIPTS`, so the positional uses `SCRIPTS[3]` and `SCRIPTS[10]` still name fanuc and tormach (work_offset_index.rs:272-273).
- Clean-room: both script headers cite public control documentation. The declaration comments point to it. No vendor post text was used.
- The decision file matches the `docs/decisions/README.md` format. The PR body has a `Changelog:` line and names issue #1385 with a closing keyword. No golden or snapshot files changed.

**Notes (not defects)**
1. The PR body says `Process change: yes`. `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` is not in the AGENTS.md process-file list. The line is harmless, but the bump rule will ignore this PR.
2. For a legacy stream with a lowercase word, for example `g55`, the two posts now write `G55`. The old path passed the string as written. The new output is the safe direction.

No new issues filed. The merge is sound.
